title: ops-sync-for-leadership-2026-03-24
content:
Cross-team engineering leadership staff sync — 2026-03-24
Owner: Priya Nair
Attendees: Priya Nair (platform), Evan Brooks (serving runtime), Zoe Martin (SRE), Daniel Chu (private deploys), Lena Kim (observability), + guests: Sarah (dedicated), Marco (devexp)

Goals for this meeting:
- Triage current operational debt items that impact SLA for hosted API and Dedicated customers
- Align on capacity run-rate for next 90 days and immediate burst strategy for Q2 launch wave
- Decide owner/resolution path for recurring KV-cache eviction incidents

1) Quick updates (2–3 min per team)
- Serving runtime (Evan): rolling kernel bump went out to 20% yesterday. Early metrics: 6% token throughput improvement on p2-small tests, but one regression on 1k+ seq tail latency in a narrow config. Investigating. Patch PR: github.com/.../pull/1017 (linked).
- Platform infra (Priya): autoscaler policy change tested in staging; aggressive scale-down causing cold-starts in low-traffic windows — observed few customer errors. Rolling back scale-down to previous threshold while we add hysteresis.
- Dedicated (Sarah): two new enterprise contracts in negotiation; need predictable 99.9 latency profile commitment. Asking eng leads for a formal SLA doc by next Wed.
- Private Deployments (Daniel): on-prem package test with customer X revealed KMS integration timing issue; encryption handoff deferred, working with security.
- Observability (Lena): new trace-sampling toggle in console is live; will help root-cause long-tail. Need product to wire up one more route for Dedicated customers.
- SRE (Zoe): incident backlog down 12% but KV-cache eviction repeats (see below). Pager rotation gap next week — will need voluntary coverage.

2) Incident deep-dive: KV-cache eviction (owner: Evan)
- Symptom: periodic mass KV cache invalidations leading to increased token compute and 2–5x latency for affected requests for ~30–90s windows.
- Recent pattern: appears during combined autoscaler + kernel bump rollouts. Hypothesis: cache shard reassign + node restart race.
- Immediate mitigation agreed: add pre-drain cache warm-up step before decommissioning nodes; delay kernel bump rollout until warm-up successful. Priya/Evan to coordinate.
- Action items:
  - Evan: implement warm-up handshake (PR due 2026-03-29) — JIRA-1987
  - Priya: change autoscaler decommission threshold to add 6m hysteresis (rollback already applied; permanent change planned by 2026-03-27)
  - Zoe: add an SLO-alert that triggers when KV eviction rate > 0.5% per minute (due 2026-03-26)

3) Capacity and cost posture (owner: Priya)
- Q2 projections: hosted API demand +12% month-over-month; Dedicated committed capacity expected +30% after two pending deals.
- Risk: current spot-based burst capacity not reliable for 48h sustained traffic spike. Need committed reserve plan.
- Temporary strategy: enable cross-region fallback and controlled overprovision (reserve 10% buffer in core regions) through Dedicated pool borrowing. Finance has okayed short-term spend increase for 6 weeks.
- Action: Priya to send an updated capacity plan and cost impact to execs by 2026-03-26. Linked JIRA-2045.

4) Rollouts & gating (owner: Evan + Marco)
- Discussion about current rollout policy: canary by traffic percent + timeframe; we need an additional gating dimension based on KV-cache churn and tail-latency percentile.
- Decision: require new kernel rollouts to be blocked by KV-cache eviction rate and 99.9th latency improvement in canary for 48h window. Marco to update rollout docs in Console by 2026-03-31.

5) Private deployments and compliance alignment (owner: Daniel + Security)
- Customer X KMS failure: short-term workaround: fall back to local KMS shim for on-prem tests while longer solution in security backlog. Security to prioritize.
- Compliance ask: enterprise legal wants export controls checklist for private package. Daniel to produce checklist draft by 2026-04-02.

6) Observability & alert noise (owner: Lena)
- Observability team proposes tag-based alert routing so Dedicated customers' alerts go to a different priority queue. Agreed in principle. Lena to prototype and demo week of 2026-03-30.
- Also propose a “cost-of-alerting” dashboard to quantify noisy alerts vs actionable ones.

7) Cross-team project syncs (fast signals)
- Model quantization pilot (Optimize team): needs infra slot for 2-week smoke test. Priya to allocate pool on 2026-04-05.
- Developer Experience (Marco): new SDK churn — ask to buy 2 engineer-weeks to stabilize streaming client. Approved; Marco to assign.

8) Open decisions and escalations
- SLA draft for Dedicated customers: need sign-off from eng leads by 2026-03-31. Sarah to coordinate.
- Cold-start problem: longer-term work to implement prefix warm caches; SRE + Serving Runtime to propose architecture by 2026-04-09.

9) Action items (concrete)
- Evan: PR for cache warm-up handshake (due 2026-03-29) — JIRA-1987
- Priya: permanent autoscaler hysteresis change and capacity plan to execs (due 2026-03-27 & 2026-03-26) — JIRA-2045
- Zoe: SLO alert for KV eviction >0.5%/min (due 2026-03-26)
- Marco: update rollout gating doc in Console with KV/latency gates (due 2026-03-31)
- Daniel: KMS checklist for Private package (draft due 2026-04-02)
- Lena: prototype tag-based alert routing demo (week of 2026-03-30)
- Sarah: circulate Dedicated SLA draft for review (due 2026-03-31)

10) Notes to follow-up in Slack:
- Thread: eng-ops #thread12345 for rollout gating discussion
- Confluence: link to updated incident runbook when warm-up handshake PR merges

Parking lot / items for next meeting:
- Long-term plan for cold-starts (architecture deep-dive)
- Automated chaos test for cache shard reassigns
- Cost-per-token benchmarking after quantization pilot

Meeting close: agreed to run smaller focused working groups for kernel rollouts and capacity; next full leadership staff sync 2026-03-31 at 10:00 PT.

Raw notes / scratch (brain-dump):
- Hypothesis: warm-up handshake should include prefetch of top-10k prefixes and patch KV versioning to avoid invalidation storms.
- Question: do we need per-customer cache tenancy for Dedicated customers? Pros: isolation. Cons: cost spike. Put in backlog.
- Quick ask: can product put a toggle in Console to temporarily disable autoscale aggressive mode? Marco to check feasibility.

---
